findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext within the instance user_data script, which is stored in Terraform state and often visible in the EC2 instance metadata service to anyone with local access, exposing long-lived AWS credentials.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative access to the entire internet.

The security group allows inbound TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0. While intended for a public web server, combined with unrestricted SSH and egress this significantly widens the attack surface with no additional layered controls.
The security group permits all outbound traffic (protocol -1, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, which allows a compromised instance to exfiltrate data or communicate freely with any external host.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, leaving data at rest unencrypted and vulnerable to exposure if the underlying storage is accessed improperly.

The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs does not configure server-side encryption, potentially exposing sensitive network traffic metadata if the bucket contents are accessed by unauthorized parties.

findings.issue_category: missing access controls / public access block
findings.description: The S3 bucket has no public access block, bucket policy, or ACL restrictions defined, risking unintended public exposure of flow log data containing network traffic details.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of the EC2 instance hosting sensitive data directly to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IP addresses to any instance launched in this subnet, expanding the network attack surface unnecessarily.
